title: Plate Tectonics, Rocks and Climate Evidence
subject: science

sections.body: Earth's crust is split into PLATES that move a few centimetres a year. Where they meet: earthquakes, volcanoes and mountains (the Himalayas formed as the Indian plate pushed into Asia).
The ROCK CYCLE: IGNEOUS rocks form from cooled magma, SEDIMENTARY from layers of sediment, METAMORPHIC from rocks changed by heat and pressure.

CLIMATE EVIDENCE: thermometer records since the 1800s, ice cores (trapped air bubbles show past CO₂), shrinking glaciers and rising sea levels. Together, they show recent warming linked to human activity.

hints: The Andes formed where an ocean plate pushes under South America. Plate collisions build mountains.
quiz.explain: The Indian plate pushing into the Eurasian plate pushed the Himalayas up.

options: Trapping air bubbles that show past atmosphere
hints: Tiny pockets of very old air.
Tree rings record past growth. Ice layers record something about the air.
quiz.explain: Air bubbles in ice cores show what the atmosphere (including CO₂) was like long ago.

quiz.q: Basalt forms when lava from a volcano cools and hardens. What type of rock is it?
hints: Think about what basalt was before it was rock: melted rock.
The lesson links one rock type to cooled magma (lava is magma that has reached the surface).
Marble forms when limestone is changed by heat and pressure, so marble is metamorphic.
quiz.explain: Rocks that form from cooled magma or lava are igneous, so basalt is an igneous rock.
